prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1478; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Evidence goes against the account: a nearby camera shows no collision at that place and time.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision and a wrist fracture. The driver is named on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 2: The police report and independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. The wrist fracture is consistent with the kind of force a frontal impact at this speed would produce.

Entry 3: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of fracture. The medical history check shows no earlier injury to the same wrist or arm.

Entry 4: The vehicle inspection shows damage on the opposite side of the front end and at a different height from the impact the claimant described. No earlier damage to the vehicle appears in our records or the prior claims search.

Entry 5: A traffic camera near the reported location shows no collision at that place and time. Requested footage and confirmation of the camera's field of view from the operator.

Entry 6: In the first call, the claimant described the direction of travel and the number of occupants differently than in the follow-up statement. Asked the claimant to clarify both points.

Entry 7: Referred the file for further review before any settlement discussion. No payment has been authorized; the claim will be reassessed once the camera footage and inspection findings are reconciled with the statements.
